newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MPC group to sell land for 20.28 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: MPC group to sell land for 20.28 bln pesos.

text.p: Fort Bonifacio Development Corp, the joint venture between a group led by Metro Pacific Corp and the government, said on Monday it signed a letter of intent for the sale of a 75 percent interest in the 64-hectare sports and recreation area within Fort Bonifacio.
The price was 20.28 billion pesos, a statement said.
The buyer was Fort McKinley Holdings Corp (FMHC) which represents a consortium of companies engaged in property development, cement manufacturing and banking.

The companies include Global Securities headed by Nora Bitong, Century Properties Inc headed by Jose Antonio, Far East Cement Corp headed by Ramon Ang, Philippine Veterans Bank, Envirocorp (Australia) Pty Ltd and other firms.
Fort Bonifacio is a prime piece of land located at the edge of the premiere financial district of Makati.
Metro Pacific, the local flagship unit of First Pacific Co Ltd, led a consortium in January 1995 which won the right to develop a 214-hectare site in Fort Bonifacio with the government.

Under the proposed sale, an initial payment of 10.14 billion pesos, representing 50 percent of the consideration, will be made in the second or third quarter of 1997. The balance will be fully secured and is to be paid with interest over a period of 75 months, the statement said.
The 64-hectare sports and recreation area includes an area of 48-hectares which will be converted into an 18-hole golf course, clubhouse and a sports and country club complex.
The remaining 16 hectares will contain residential, commercial, sports and recreational facilities.

"The progress made by Fort Bonifacio Development Corp (FBDC) since award of the development in early 1995 has demonstrated the soundness of the investment by its shareholders," said Ricardo Pascua, president and chief executive officer of FBDC.
In 1996, 16 hectares of developed land were sold at an average price of about 180,000 pesos per square metre compared with the acquisiton price of 33,288 pesos per square metre, he said.
The 1996 sales generated potential revenues of 28 billion pesos and yielded a net income of over one billion pesos for FBDC.
The latest sale valued the undeveloped land at 42,250 pesos per square metre, the statement said.
